record_body:
Account summary (ABM FinServ):
- Wealth mgmt arm of larger financial group. Early signal: strong appetite for “Hosted → Dedicated → Private” story, but starting point is Private/VPC due to policy.
- Primary goal: replace a patchwork of internal model endpoints + vendor APIs with a consistent inference layer (latency/cost predictable + auditability).

Key contacts (from discovery + emails):
- VP Platform Engineering (technical sponsor) — owns VPC networking + internal service mesh.
- Director, InfoSec (security gate) — pushing for log/audit story + key mgmt.
- GRC manager (questionnaire owner).
- Applied ML lead (success criteria for quality + throughput).

Discovery findings (what we heard):
- Current state:
  - Mix of Azure OpenAI (for some teams) + internal GPU cluster experiments (vLLM). “We’re spending more time operating than building.”
  - Complaints: unpredictable latency during peak advisor hours; cost spikes when prompts get long; no unified audit trail across vendors.
- Target workloads (POC candidate #1):
  - Advisor-assist chat + retrieval over internal research PDFs and client notes (embeddings + reranking).
  - Output must be constrained/structured for downstream systems (CRM notes + compliance tags).
- Non-negotiables:
  - Data residency: US-only. Preference for single-region control; no cross-region processing.
  - Private networking: VPC-only access from their app tier. No public egress requirement for inference path.
  - Auditability: immutable request metadata trail (who/when/which model version) + admin actions.
  - Key management: CMK via cloud KMS preferred; HSM is “nice to have” but not required for POC.
  - SSO/SAML + RBAC for Console access.
- Performance targets (initial):
  - P50 latency: <800ms to first token (streaming), P95 <2.5s for typical 1–2k token outputs.
  - Throughput: bursty traffic aligned to market hours; wants guidance on autoscaling vs reserved capacity.
- Model posture:
  - Open to Redwood-curated open models; wants fallback option if capacity constrained.
  - Asked for guidance on quantization profiles and whether quality regression is measurable (they like the evals angle).

Residency + retention notes (flagged for Security/GRC):
- Explicit question: “Do you store prompts/outputs anywhere in Private?”
  - We used approved language: in Private/VPC deployment, customer controls networking and storage boundaries; any logging/telemetry is configurable and reviewed as part of deployment.
  - Follow-up needed: document where operational logs live and what is exported to their SIEM.
- Retention:
  - They want the option to set retention to 0 for prompts/outputs (or disable) while still retaining audit metadata.
  - Need crisp explanation of what’s considered audit metadata vs payload content.

Competitive notes:
- Bedrock: appealed because ‘AWS native’ + network controls, but they’re unhappy with model/endpoint sprawl + cost predictability.
- Azure OpenAI: already used in parts of org; policy pressure to reduce third-party exposure for certain client data.
- Self-host vLLM: their ML team can run it, but platform team doesn’t want to own upgrades, kernel perf work, and reliability.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-01-09: Intro + discovery scheduled via SDR (finserv ABM sequence). Key topic: Private/VPC requirement.
- 2026-01-18: Email recap from Hannah w/ draft POC plan + requested security attendees (see thread).
- 2026-01-21: Fireflies call (POC scoping) — agreed on 2–3 week technical evaluation if security packet lands quickly.
- 2026-02-04: Platform team asked for clarity on VPC connectivity options + DNS/TLS assumptions (captured for SE follow-up).
- 2026-02-11: Internal Redwood review: align on what we can commit to re: audit log export and retention configuration (no over-promises).

Mutual Action Plan (draft) — POC + security review:
- Phase 0 — Kickoff (Week 0)
  - Redwood: send FinServ security FAQ addendum + Private/VPC reference architecture; provide list of required customer inputs (VPC CIDRs, egress policy, SSO config, SIEM endpoint).
  - Crescent: confirm POC workload owner + sample request patterns (prompt sizes, expected output length), confirm ‘US-only’ region requirement.
- Phase 1 — Architecture + access (Week 1)
  - Joint: 60-min architecture session (platform + security + SE) to confirm:
    - Connectivity approach (peering vs PrivateLink), DNS/TLS termination, allowed egress.
    - Logging plan: audit events + metrics export to SIEM.
    - KMS integration approach and key ownership.
  - Exit criteria: signed off network diagram + responsibilities matrix.
- Phase 2 — Technical POC (Weeks 1–2)
  - Redwood: stand up Private/VPC environment; enable streaming + structured output; configure basic dashboards.
  - Crescent: integrate one service path (advisor-assist endpoint) + provide eval prompt set; run load tests in market-hour simulation.
  - Success metrics:
    - Meet latency targets for defined prompt distributions.
    - Demonstrate routing/fallback policy (documented behavior) for capacity constraints.
    - Provide token-level cost/latency breakdown from Console for the workload.
- Phase 3 — Security review (runs in parallel; target completion by Week 3)
  - Crescent: deliver their standard security questionnaire + data flow diagram requirements.
  - Redwood (Aisha/Olga support as needed): answer questionnaire; provide SOC2 evidence under NDA; confirm audit log coverage, retention controls, and residency commitments.
  - Exit criteria: InfoSec ‘OK to proceed’ to procurement.
- Phase 4 — Commercials + procurement (Weeks 3–4)
  - Decide Dedicated vs Private contract structure for initial production slice (leaning Private).
  - Define SLOs + support tier; confirm any add-ons (observability retention, compliance package).
  - Target: paper process starts immediately after security exit.

Open questions (to resolve next call):
- Which cloud + region is mandated for US-only residency? (They hinted at AWS us-east-1 preference; not confirmed.)
- Do they require customer-managed keys on day 1 for POC or only production?
- What is their exact definition of “audit log” (admin actions only vs request-level metadata) and required export format (JSON over HTTPS vs S3 bucket delivery).

Internal notes (Redwood):
- Keep messaging tight: we can be strong on Private/VPC boundaries + auditability, but avoid implying zero data retention by default unless configured/specified.
- If PrivateLink is a hard requirement and not supported in their topology, escalate early to avoid wasted cycle.
- Recommend looping in Simran Kaur (reference architect) if they want a formal architecture doc for security sign-off.
